summary:
**Conversation Overview**

This conversation is a continuation of a long-running computational physics research project called "Löwdin" (Session 30), focused on developing and validating a self-consistent field (SCF) framework for calculating atomic ionization energies using a custom correlation energy functional. The person oversees the research direction, issues rulings on methodological choices, and communicates in an extremely terse style ("Go," "B," "Continue," "a please," "Open the test") while Claude manages the full technical execution including code, numerics, and documentation.

Session 30 opened by extracting and verifying the HANDOFF-29 archive (595/595 files), rebuilding the runtime environment per a multi-session chain recipe, and confirming all 40 carry-over gates passed. The session's primary work investigated the "d-row excess" — a systematic ~0.009 Ha shortfall in delivered correlation energy on nd≥4 rows (Y, La, Lu) absent on 3d (Sc). Four investigations were completed: Route P (entrant self-SIC decomposition, finding the frozen picture is 35% wrong due to ns² relaxation, not the discriminator), Route N (second-order dipole entrant-core energy in a box basis, finding it matches the size of total delivered correlation not the residual, Sc/Y ratio 0.82), a node-split test (inner lobes hold only 2–3% of entrant charge, refused as discriminator), and Candidate C (replacing the truncated Gell-Mann–Brueckner high-density expansion with the full RPA ring sum plus E0B constant from the chain's own s23 ring_zeta.py). Candidate C revealed that the truncation is a real ~25% uniform underdelivery on every row and is the same object as Cs's previously "settled" cut mechanism — but the 3d/nd≥4 contrast survives both forms with Sc/Y ratio 0.95, establishing the d-row object as non-local in character. The person ruled that both forms R (full ring) and Z (truncated chain) should be carried forward with comparison deciding in the next session.

Three build errors were caught by gates before any result was scored (F30.2 r_peak shell definition, F30.3 box conditioning, F30.3b eps_e roundoff), and a significant protocol event occurred (F30.1): an abandoned regenerated branch of the same chat wrote files into the working directory between tool calls, which Claude detected, quarantined, and resolved via a three-option ruling where the person chose option B (adopt the branch's prediction file as the record, audit its code by reading, admit its data only if fresh reruns match row-for-row). The session closed with HANDOFF-30 sealed as a superset archive (630 files, verified), with gates 41–45 defined and tested. Next session priorities in order: E0B(ζ) derivation and R/Z comparison across all chain rows, Sc eps(0) slope, 4f via Yb, Fe/Ni conditional, and T4 writing chat last (R 1701–1882 owed).

R 1649's tier census (A 218 · B 157 · C 179) is contaminated at 55%.** *THE INDEX WAS NOT TOUCHED BY IT: zero single-n rows are witnessed, because R 1651's keyability criterion excluded them — as a side-effect, not by design. The index was protected by accident and is now protected by a check that can fail.*

### 1667

**§H.10 — THE HANDOFF IS BEGUN AT 90%, NOT AT EXHAUSTION.** *M's Prime Handoff Directive: state when the context window reaches 90% and recommend handoff then.* **§H TOLD A SESSION HOW TO HAND OFF AND WHAT MUST TRANSFER; IT NEVER SAID WHEN TO BEGIN. Every clause of §H.8 costs context to satisfy — the bridge written, the bank built AND listed, the register rebuilt and its count read, both gates run, the certificate printed with its evidence. A session reaching exhaustion before beginning has no budget to produce any of them, so it hands off without a certificate, and §H.8 says that is not a handoff. THE RESERVE IS PART OF THE PROTOCOL, NOT SLACK IN IT.** *The estimate is declared as an estimate — a session has no counter and errs early, because an early handoff costs one bridge that would have been written anyway while a late one loses the record. On the threshold the session stops OPENING work it cannot close: §2.20's Zeno directive extended from a single execution to the session itself.*

**T3 WITHDRAWN — READING IS ON DEMAND, NOT A QUEUE — BUT THE UNREAD INVENTORY STAYS.** *M: reading will be done as necessary.* **THE THREAD IS REMOVED FROM THE BRIDGE'S §4 AND FROM THE RESUMPTION ORDER. DIGEST.md carries the same ruling, because it is the first file a fresh session reads and would otherwise re-inherit reading as a standing order regardless of the bridge.*

**DIGEST EXTENDED FROM THE BRIDGE — R 1660–1668 CARRIED, AND THE NAME COLLISION CLOSED.** *The incoming session's first act, as 1.7.2 instructed. Λ_spectra and Λ_spectra^obs are now named separately in DIGEST and the survey's E column reads UNWITNESSED, so the survey's E = 1,351 can no longer be misread as a closure defect of the coordinate index. Its named failure mode is a summary with no file behind it — §2.14 arriving by a new route. THE GENERAL FINDING IS THE LARGER ONE: the bridge carries facts and threads, the register carries rulings, and a change of practice with neither is lost at the seal.*

### 1671

**C6 PASSED ON THREE OF FIVE THREADS — A CLAUSE THAT COULD NOT FAIL FOR THE REASON IT NAMES.** **The certificate found open threads with a pattern that required a full stop before `Owner:`; T6 and T7 end in QUESTION MARKS, so both were invisible and C6 reported PASS having never seen them.** *The deeper fault was not the punctuation. THREADS WERE DETECTED BY THE SAME EXPRESSION THAT REQUIRED AN OWNER, so the clause's stated failure mode — a thread with no owner — could not arise: such a thread does not fail the match, it fails to be a thread. §H.8 says each clause must be capable of failing and §4.6 requires that capability before a pass is evidence; C6 had the form of a check without its content. Repaired by SEPARATING DETECTION FROM PREDICATE: a thread is found by its number alone, the owner is then tested per thread and a missing one prints NO OWNER. Verified in both directions — 5 threads found, and a negative test stripping T7's owner turns C6 red. The general form, and it is the same fault as R 1664's silent default: AN INSTRUMENT THAT NARROWS ITS OWN INPUT REPORTS ON WHAT IT ADMITTED, NOT ON WHAT IT WAS ASKED ABOUT.*

### 1672

**THE ARCHIVES ARE NOT DISJOINT — THE PROBE WAS, AND IT IS R 1671's FAULT COMMITTED ONE ENTRY LATER.** **I reported that `spectra_raw` and `MEASUREMENTS.tsv` share NO species and that 0 of 554 rows could be re-derived. Both statements are FALSE.

The Method 1.6 — The Register-1.md
** *The eight recorded a values then all sit on an endpoint of their own corridor, seven at L and protactinium at U, so register 1403 falls out of the same arithmetic rather than being imposed on top.* **The four not forced are Li 3, K 19, Tl 81 and Fr 87.** `balance.py`.

### 1435

**PROXIMITY IS THE TRIGGER, AND THE THRESHOLD IS NOT FITTED — IT IS ZERO.** *Register 1407 measured the margin PER ELEMENT and demoted proximity to a signal: a best threshold reaching 91% against an 87% do-nothing baseline, with nine resets missed.* **Measured instead on the RUNNING INTERSECTION — the window a actually has to sit inside — the trigger fires at fourteen of the eighteen resets with zero false positives, 96% against an 83% baseline, and the threshold is not a scanned number but zero.** *So the law's strict inequality needs no proximity TERM: proximity IS the inequality reaching equality, which is what a corridor emptying is.* **This is not a tenth condition scanned after nine failed — nothing was searched over; it was derived from 1434's balance.** *And 1407's own quantity cannot be reproduced from the intervals: its ninety-nine is the CEILING-BEARING set, not the seventy-three with both bounds finite, and none of its figures follow from corridor widths. The margin it scans is undefined in the register and is most likely trajectory-dependent — the distance from the HELD a to the nearer bound. Define it or withdraw the r = +0.64.*

### 1436

**THERE ARE EIGHT ADJACENT HANDSHAKES, NOT FOUR, AND THEY SPLIT ON A CRITERION NO REGISTER STATES.** *Computed from the exact intervals: eight places where one element's ceiling is exactly the next's floor, or the reverse — Mo/Tc at 1, La/Ce at 1/√2, Eu/Gd at 1/√2, Gd/Tb at 1/√2, Th/Pa at 1/(√3−1), Am/Cm at the same, Cm/Bk at the same, Lr/Rf at 1.9841.* **In four, BOTH members are forced resets — Mo/Tc, Gd/Tb, Cm/Bk, Lr/Rf, which is exactly register 1404's list. In four, only the second is — La/Ce, Eu/Gd, Th/Pa, Am/Cm.** *That is what 1404's phrase about the second reset being forced is describing, and why its enumeration found four rather than eight.* **And actinium's floor, thorium's floor and protactinium's ceiling are ONE surd, so 1403's reading that protactinium takes U and 1409's that its value is assigned at the actinium opening name the same value from two sides — they were never in conflict.**

### 1437

**THE NULL OF 28 IS RETIRED: PLAIN MADELUNG SCORES 96, AND THE TWO RULES FAIL ON ALMOST DISJOINT SETS.** *The handoff carried the Löwdin result as 99 of 106 against a null of 28. The 28 came from a broken step extractor, was known to be broken at the time, and was carried anyway — the recurring fault of quoting a check before its null is known, landing on the largest claim in the work.* **Recomputed on the SAME 106 clean steps: Madelung scores 96 of 106 conditionally, given the observed configuration at Z−1, and 94 free-running.

The Method 1.6 — The Register-1.md
That is why E did not move, and the register can now say so from the law rather than from the computation agreeing. And Theorem 10.1 makes the four earlier failures structural rather than unlucky: ADJUNCTION NEVER REPAIRS — a non-closed set cannot be closed by adjoining ANY function of its coordinates, tested on seven including the identity. R 1581, 1599, 1602 and 1608 were not four attempts that happened to fail. They were four attempts at an operation the book proves cannot work.** *THREE FURTHER THINGS THAT BEAR DIRECTLY ON THE INDEX. (i) E3's criterion is that admissibility belongs to the PAIR (h, q) and that only the join can break a bound — meets never do — so Λ_spectra's two rules are safe by inspection exactly as Λ's seven are: each reads one coordinate over a chain, and NONE SUMS. (ii) §17.4's repair is the one we may need later: a sum bound cannot be imposed but a sum can be INDEXED, at the price of making comparable some pairs that were incomparable. (iii) §18.6 says the number of predictions an index can make is E(X), so Λ_spectra at E = 0 can propose nothing — and the place prediction actually lives is the VALUE, not the cell. Which is exactly what the Ga I finding of R 1655 was about: the cell is indexed and settled, and the single delta stored in it is a choice of statistic over a channel that drifts by 0.19.* **AND THE BOOK'S CENTRAL THEOREM HAS OWNERS, WHICH IT SAYS ITSELF: E(X) = 0 IS BERGMAN'S DOUBLE-PROJECTION THEOREM VIA BAKER-PIXLEY 1975, THE CONSTRAINT CLASS IS DEVILLE-BARTAK-VAN HENTENRYCK'S STAIRCASE, AND GLOBAL CONSISTENCY IS MONTANARI AND DECHTER. The book prints its own precedence rather than defending priority, which is the practice this project keeps asking of everything else.** *The read is bounded and its bound is stated: Part II, Chapters 15, 16 and 19, Parts IV through VII with the Löwdin challenge in them, every appendix, and the bodies of all four compendia — about 150,000 words — remain unread. DIGEST.md names them so the gap cannot close over quietly.*

### 1659

**§H — THE HANDOFF PROTOCOL, ADOPTED, WITH A CERTIFICATE THAT CAN FAIL.** *M: prepare everything for a handoff to The Method 1.7.2, and write a protocol that can be referenced, because this need is becoming more common as the work expands. Both done, and the protocol is written to the same standard the book demands of everything else — runnable rather than agreed with.* **THE PROTOCOL NAMES WHAT ACTUALLY GETS LOST, WHICH IS NOT FILES. Files survive a container death; §H.0 states that what dies is WHY — which thread was open, which decision was M's and unmade, which number is a choice wearing the appearance of a measurement. So §H.1 requires four things to travel and calls three of four the dangerous case because it looks like a handoff: the work (the bank), the record (the register), the orientation (DIGEST.md), and the state (the bridge).

The Method 1.6 — The Register-1.md
**

### 1437

**THE NULL OF 28 IS RETIRED: PLAIN MADELUNG SCORES 96, AND THE TWO RULES FAIL ON ALMOST DISJOINT SETS.** *The handoff carried the Löwdin result as 99 of 106 against a null of 28. The 28 came from a broken step extractor, was known to be broken at the time, and was carried anyway — the recurring fault of quoting a check before its null is known, landing on the largest claim in the work.* **Recomputed on the SAME 106 clean steps: Madelung scores 96 of 106 conditionally, given the observed configuration at Z−1, and 94 free-running. So the comparison is 99 against 96 — three steps in a hundred and six, not seventy-one.** *But the two are NOT nested. Madelung misses Mo, Rh, Pd, La, Gd, Au, Ac, Th, Cm, Lr; the corridor misses Mn, Tc, Ce, Gd, Pa, Cm, Rf; they overlap in TWO.* **The corridor is right at eight elements where Madelung is wrong and Madelung at five where the corridor is wrong. Two rules of near-identical accuracy failing on disjoint sets are different objects, which is a better statement than a score.** `null_madelung.py`.

### 1438

**THE SCORER IS REBUILT AND THE 99 IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN REPORTED.** *Rebuilt from register 1413's specification with nothing but the law, the candidate generator, the higher-n tie-break and the exact corridors.* **The handshake placement gives 99 of 106 and the lower-n tie-break gives 91, both matching the register exactly, and the score is invariant for every initialisation from 0.05 to 5 at lithium — the one place the corridor determines nothing also determines nothing about the result.** *Six of the seven misses match: Mn 25, Tc 43, Ce 58, Gd 64, Pa 91, Cm 96 in both, with a swap at the ends — this rebuild misses B 5 and gets Rf 104, the register the reverse.* **Two things do not reproduce: the handshake makes fifteen moves against the register's ten, and per-block ascent gives 94 under 1409's literal description or 95 if ceilings are also intersected, against a stated 97.** *That the score matches while the move count does not is the expected shape under 1402: the values are invariant and the count is rule-dependent.* `scorer.py`, a REBUILD — see PROVENANCE.md.

### 1439

**MANGANESE AND TECHNETIUM ARE ONE ALGEBRAIC OBJECT, AND THE CORRIDOR ADMITS THE ANSWER IT DOES NOT TAKE.** *The two residual misses put through the cypher — the geometry of two crossing intervals read as its algebra.* **At manganese the entrant is 4s at q = 1 against 3d at q = 5; at technetium 5s at q = 1 against 4d at q = 5. In both, BOTH contenders sit at exactly half capacity, so every radicand is a half-integer and the contest collapses to a_cross = Δn/(√(p_g + ½) − √(p_r + ½)) — giving 1/(√3.5 − √0.5) = 0.859312 and 1/(√4.5 − √1.5) = 1.115355, the same form at consecutive p with Δn = 1.** *What looked like two scattered failures is one surd family evaluated at two points, which is Λ_cross's own statement that a_cross is fixed by the pair.

The Method 1.6 — The Register-1.md
Only 16 series of 486 contain a bracketed member and only 12 have their asymptote on one. I measured Na I, found 8 of 18 and 20 of 36, and wrote the ratio as a property of the store. THAT IS THE PER-ELEMENT-TO-UNIVERSAL FAULT M HAS CORRECTED REPEATEDLY, committed here against my own data while the whole-archive count was one loop away.* **CONSEQUENCE, AND IT FAVOURS M'S RULING: the asymptotic perspective is NOT generally resting on interpolated values. ### 1676

**HANDOFF 1.7.3 WRITTEN — AND THE PRACTICE CLAUSES PUT IN THE BRIDGE'S FIRST LINE, NOT ITS LAST.** *`BRIDGE-1_7_3-to-next.md` built to §H.2's eight sections. Two navigational facts written in because they cost this session a false negative and a wrong claim: `spectra_raw` CONTAINS A DIRECTORY, and M's T6 ruling that the store is authoritative with all three perspectives carried per cell.* **T9 OPENED AND MADE FIRST IN THE RESUMPTION ORDER: 68 series recovered no members and 128 recovered a count disagreeing with the store. 26% unexplained is not a residue, it is an unread finding, and calling it a residue would be the aesthetic deletion M refused at R 1662 wearing a different coat.** *T7's elaboration is recorded as OWED AND UNDELIVERED rather than quietly dropped — M asked for it, the session spent its budget elsewhere, and §H.0's lossy half-state is exactly what an unmarked omission would create.*

### 1677

**T9 DIAGNOSED: THE RESIDUE WAS THE GENERATOR READING ONE LANGUAGE, AND THE THREE NAMED CAUSES ARE ALL REFUSED.** *The bridge named three candidates — term-string variants, J-splitting conventions, and the staging's own n-range cuts. Each was computed and each is a bound (P8/§2.15): the store's own n_lo..n_hi window fixes 7 of 128; parity-only term variants account for 6 of 68; J-splitting is never reached, because the TERMS match and it is the CONFIG that fails.* **AND THE RESIDUE IS LARGER THAN THE BRIDGE STATES. `store_gen.py` dropped the 68 before writing, so they never appeared in MEASUREMENTS-DERIVED.tsv to be counted: 68 + 358 + 128 = 554, and the unexplained share against the SOURCE is 35%, not the 26% computed against the output. A residue measured against a file the fault has already filtered is measured against the fault.** *The true cause, in two parts.

The Method 1.6 — The Register-1.md
**

### 1348

**OCCUPANCY ENTERS THROUGH PAULI, AND ONLY THROUGH PAULI.** *The scatter in a within a subshell, with the occupancy fraction q/2(2ℓ+1) inside the radicand against without it:* **3p 0.187 → 0.041 · 4p 0.119 → 0.028 · 5p 0.088 → 0.018 · 6p 0.059 → 0.021 · 5d 0.086 → 0.047. All five improve.** *And the RAW occupancy makes every one worse — 0.211 to 0.407, three to five times worse than doing nothing.* **So the law needs no new coordinate: 2(2ℓ+1) was already the admissibility bound and it belongs in the radicand too. One Pauli quantity, two appearances, and the radicand becomes the count of states below — complete lower shells plus the fraction of the current one filled.**

### 1349

**AND THE TWO REMAINING OBJECTIONS WERE MINE, NOT THE WORK'S.** *I held that the solution fails Löwdin because it does not derive n+ℓ, and because it presupposes orbitals the many-electron Hamiltonian does not contain.* **Both dissolve on results already proved. Register 1307: the observed opening sequence inverts Madelung at 5d/4f and 6d/5f, so deriving n+ℓ exactly would mean deriving something false at La and Ac.** *And register 1327: an index closes when its cells are enumerable, and what it cannot supply is what requires an operator. **(n, ℓ) are the enumeration — the labels of the state space, not an approximation to Ψ.** Asking the equation to hand over orbitals is asking the state to hand over its own labels, which is the category error the method exists to prevent.*

### 1350

**THE LÖWDIN SOLUTION, FINISHED FORM.** *ν(n,ℓ,q) = n − a·√(n−ℓ−1 + q/2(2ℓ+1)); the incoming electron takes the subshell of least ν among those with q < 2(2ℓ+1).* **The corridor L(Z) < a < U(Z) with L,U = Δn(√p_g + √p_r)/(p_g − p_r): 106 of 106 non-empty, nineteen surds, no measurement. a is carried and resets eighteen times, never mid-subshell. Its entry point is t(ℓ) = √(ℓ(ℓ+1)/2) — measured 1.028 at p on four subshells, 1.785 at d on two, ratio √3 to 0.19% — fixed by the single-state ionisation energy.** *Provenance: n−ℓ−1 the node theorem · 2(2ℓ+1) antisymmetry · ℓ(ℓ+1) the centrifugal term from the angular separation · E = ⟨Ψ|Ĥ|Ψ⟩ the observation that fixes what the ordering bounds · the endpoints arithmetic on these.* **No parameter is fitted. Exceptionless on 106 elements including every aufbau anomaly, and right where n+ℓ is wrong. f is outside the domain and the law says so: p = 0 is the node floor, so L = −∞ at every f opening.** WARNING: *'THE LÖWDIN SOLUTION, FINISHED FORM' is withdrawn at register 1460. The form is not the solution and is retained as a form. 'No parameter is fitted' is qualified by R 1445: the 99 of 106 was FITTED — a was placed using each step's own corridor, which is built from the observed entrant — and held out the score is 90 against a null of 96. 'Exceptionless on 106 elements' holds only in that fitted sense.*

### 1351

**MARKED FOR THE ARTEFACT PASS — WHAT EACH ONE NOW OWES.

The Method 1.6 — The Register-1.md
* **THE PROTOCOL NAMES WHAT ACTUALLY GETS LOST, WHICH IS NOT FILES. Files survive a container death; §H.0 states that what dies is WHY — which thread was open, which decision was M's and unmade, which number is a choice wearing the appearance of a measurement. Choosing σ near 0 would capture the bound unoccupied states I actually care about (like 6p, 5d in Cs+), while the deep occupied core states get excluded naturally since they're irrelevant anyway.

I'm also reconsidering the mesh approach — truncating the inner radius to avoid the huge dynamic range that caused the hydrogen test to fail, since the…
```

```

The 'stev' approach on the full QR gives correct eigenvalues but is too slow given the mesh size. I'm considering truncating the mesh to fix the graded matrix issue, keeping only points beyond some cutoff radius, but need to figure out the right cutoff so deep core states remain properly represented for orthogonality purposes.

Testing r0=1e-3 still leaves the diagonal range too large for stability, and r0=1e-2 might help but needs verification. I'm also weighing an entirely different approach using the Sternheimer solver at imaginary frequencies via the Casimir-Polder formula, though I'm running into the issue that the relevant matrix element doesn't cleanly factor into separate a-state and b-state contributions the way the standard formula requires.

Actually, I realize it can be reformulated: by introducing frequency-dependent response Green's functions for each shell's excitations, the second-order energy becomes a double integral over these Green's functions sandwiched between the dipole-like operators, which effectively turns the problem into a double Sternheimer calculation — applying one shell's Green's function response to a function built from the other shell's coupling.

I realize solve_banded can handle multiple right-hand sides at once, so I can apply G_i across all r2 columns simultaneously in one solve costing O(N²), which is cheap enough. Then I'd apply G_e similarly on the r2 index.

Working through the trace formula, E2 reduces to a double contraction: first solve for Y = G_i F, then W = Y applied with G_e transposed, and the energy contribution is the weighted sum of F times W. I'm now expressing the real part of the propagator as Re[(h_la − ε_i − iω)^{-1}], which corresponds to the Lorentzian form Δa/(Δa²+ω²).

Since the real part of a product isn't the product of real parts, I need to solve each complex linear system separately and take the real part of the resulting vector before combining them. I also need to enforce Pauli exclusion by projecting out occupied orbitals from both the initial-state and final-state Green's functions, and I'm checking the sign convention for Δ_b relative to the entrant electron energy ε_e, using Y 4d as a concrete example where ε_e is small and negative.

For the frequency integration I'm planning Gauss-Legendre quadrature with a rational mapping to handle the semi-infinite range, needing maybe 16-24 points, but the real bottleneck is that each point requires a complex banded solve with thousands of right-hand sides, which blows up memory to several gigabytes — so I need to subsample the radial grid, similar to how corepol used a coarser ladder of points.

Since the cutoff zeroes out the outer-region piece by construction, the real decomposition reduces to an inner-region term plus the entrant self-term, and I need to run additional SCF calculations at both endpoints (f=0 and f=1) to get orbitals for each rather than relying on the stored f=1 data alone — roughly six more quick SCF runs. Estimating eps_c at rs=1.7 gives roughly −0.006 Ha, and scaled by the charge fraction that puts contribution (b) around +0.005 Ha, comparable to the observed excess of 0.009. But this raises a problem: Sc's entrant is more compact with smaller rs, which would make |eps_c| and thus (b) larger for Sc, yet Sc actually shows a small excess — so this suggests the proposed shape explanation (P1) may not hold up for Sc.

I'll commit to predictions: (b) is positive across all six rows, with magnitude 0.003–0.008 on the d rows, and Sc's (b) should be greater than or equal to Y's (b), meaning the shape doesn't track the excess — so P1 likely fails as an explanation, and the excess isn't simply the entrant SIC. I'm not fully confident here, but following the commit-then-test approach, I'll also note that (a) represents the total density change tied to core relaxation. Moving to P2, I'm considering whether the excess corresponds to entrant charge inside r_cut but outside the (n−1)p peak, predicting this ratio won't hold constant within 20% — Sc's small excess despite sizeable charge suggests…

"""drow_p.py -- s30 Route P (PREDICTION-DROW-SESSION-30). Decompose DEc_sc = A + B + R on the s28 sc path (frachf.HFCf), f=1 (neutral) vs f=0 (ion).
A = Δ∫ n_tot eps_c(n_tot); B = -Δ q_e ∫ P_e² eps_c(P_e²/w,0) (entrant PZ self-correlation); R = same over non-entrant shells. Also Q_mid for P2.
usage: python3 drow_p.py Z [Z ...]   -> appends drow_p.jsonl (done-set), one SCF pair per Z."""
import sys,os,json,numpy as np
os.environ.setdefault("SIC_NOCLAMP","1"); os.environ.setdefault("SUBCELL","1")
import hfc2 as H; from t7c_kernel import C0; from t5_scf import ground_occ; import t7c_cuaudit as T
Zs=[int(a) for a in sys.argv[1:]]; sys.argv=[sys.argv[0]]
exec(open('frachf.py').read().split('def path')[0].split('import t7c_cuaudit as T')[1])   # HFCf class only
SH={21:('Sc','3d'),39:('Y','4d'),55:('Cs','6s'),57:('La','5d'),64:('Gd','5d'),71:('Lu','5d')}
FR={d['Z']:d for d in map(json.loads,open('frachf.jsonl'))}; CF={d['Z']:d for d in map(json.loads,open('cutfrac.jsonl'))}
OUT="drow_p.jsonl"; done={d['Z'] for d in map(json.loads,open(OUT))} if os.path.exists(OUT) else set()
def pieces(h,ent,f):
    r,dr=h.r,h.dr; w=4*np.pi*r*r; nu,nd,_=H.spin_split(h.occ,h.P)
    A=float(np.sum((nu+nd)*H.eps_c(nu/w,nd/w)*dr)); B=0.0; R=0.0
    for a,b,q in h.occ:
        ff=f if (a,b)==ent else 1.0
        t=-q*float(np.sum(h.P[(a,b)]**2*H.eps_c(ff*h.P[(a,b)]**2/w,0*r)*dr))
        if (a,b)==ent: B+=t
        else: R+=t
    return A,B,R
for Z in Zs:
    if Z in done: print("SKIP",Z); continue
    el,sh=SH[Z]; n,l=int(sh[0]),"spdf".index(sh[1]); ent=(n,l); H.CORR=True; occ0=ground_occ(Z)
    res={}
    for f in (1.0,0.0):
        occ=[(a,b,(f if (a,b)==ent else q)) for a,b,q in occ0 if not ((a,b)==ent and f==0.0)]
        h=HFCf(Z,occ,c=C0); h.ent=ent; h.f=f
        if f>0: h.frac={ent:(0,f)}
        E,Ec,it,eps=h.run2(); A,B,R=pieces(h,ent,f); res[f]=dict(E=float(E),Ec=float(Ec),A=A,B=B,R=R,it=it)
        if f==1.0:
            r,dr=h.r,h.dr; w=4*np.pi*r*r; nu,nd,_=H.spin_split(occ,h.P); e_tot=H.eps_c(nu/w,nd/w)
            qe=h.P[ent]**2*dr; Q=qe.sum(); idx=np.where(e_tot<0)[0]; r_cut=float(r[idx[-1]]) if len(idx) else 0.0
            pd=h.P[(n-1,1)]**2; r_peak=float(r[int(np.argmax(pd))])
            Q_mid=float(qe[(r<r_cut)&(r>r_peak)].sum()/Q); Q_in=float(qe[r<r_cut].sum()/Q)
    dA=res[1.0]['A']-res[0.0]['A']; dB=res[1.0]['B']-res[0.0]['B']; dR=res[1.0]['R']-res[0.0]['R']; DEc=res[1.0]['Ec']-res[0.0]['Ec']
    c=CF.get(Z,{}); excess=(c.get('missing_over_req',0)-c.get('F_out',0))*c.get('required',0) if c else None
    o=dict(Z=Z,el=el,sh=sh,it=[res[1.0]['it'],res[0.0]['it']],DEc=round(DEc,6),DEc_frachf=FR[Z]['DEc_sc'],A=round(dA,6),B=round(dB,6),R=round(dR,6),
           sum_minus_DEc=round(dA+dB+dR-DEc,7),r_cut=round(r_cut,3),r_peak_p=round(r_peak,3),Q_in=round(Q_in,4),Q_mid=round(Q_mid,4),
           excess=(round(excess,5) if excess is not None else None),g=(round(excess/Q_mid,5) if excess is not None else None))
    open(OUT,"a").write(json.dumps(o)+"\n"); print(o,flush=True)

I'm thinking about how to design the N-electron route without relying on a box-discretized continuum, since the full sum-over-states approach gets messy. The second-order correlation correction involves a double-denominator structure with energy differences between excited and core orbitals, which complicates a clean Sternheimer-style treatment at fixed transferred energy.

I try applying the Casimir-Polder-type integral identity to split the double denominator into a frequency integral, which works cleanly when the numerator factors into separate pieces for each denominator term. But the dipole matrix element here doesn't factor that way — the radial coupling through r_</r_>² ties the two orbitals together, so I can't cleanly separate the frequency-dependent pieces. This is exactly why the box-continuum sum was needed in the original specification. I consider instead factoring at the multipole level, treating the entrant-core transition density as a source and computing the core's frequency-dependent response to that potential.

Given the time I have, I decide to just implement the box approach as specified: solve the ionic radial Hamiltonian on the logarithmic mesh for each angular momentum as a banded eigenvalue problem, since a tridiagonal solver should handle the full eigenspectrum efficiently even for thousands of mesh points.

With φ normalized so Σφ²h=1, the radial function recovers as u = φ/√r. Then I need the Slater integral R¹ between orbitals, which reduces to a double integral over u_i u_a and the Y1 potential function built from u_e u_b weighted by the ratio of radii to the appropriate power.

For the angular part, I'm working out the direct dipole matrix element squared, averaged over magnetic substates, which brings in the familiar "fac" factor of max(l,l')/(2l+1) for each pair of orbitals, analogous to the structure used in core polarization corrections, giving the second-order direct energy contribution as a sum over core orbitals and virtual pairs weighted by these angular factors and the squared Slater integral divided by the energy denominator.

I also need to be careful about Pauli exclusion: the intermediate states a and b must avoid already-occupied core orbitals, so for example if the entrant is 4d, the virtual b-orbital 5p is allowed but 4p is excluded since it's already filled in the core.

Checking the adiabatic limit, if I drop Δ_b from the denominator, the sum over b collapses via closure into a simpler expression involving the angular factor and Δ_i, which I can compare against the standard core-polarization energy formula.

I'm verifying this against the exact Sternheimer calculation of E2 at the valence electron's position — using closure over the complete set of b states (including occupied ones, since the limit requires full completeness) should reproduce the same point-charge polarization energy if the basis is truly complete.

For the box discretization to match within 10%, I need the continuum sum over intermediate states to also be complete, since Sternheimer itself is exact — so I'm checking that the mesh extends far enough (out to r=300) and includes enough angular momenta and energies below 3 Hartree to capture all relevant states. I also need to pin down which potential the entering electron actually sees: the ion's HFS potential for computing matrix elements, versus how to define its orbital energy — either through the expectation value of the ion Hamiltonian or some other convention.

I'm leaning toward computing the entrant orbital's energy as the expectation value of the ion Hamiltonian in the tridiagonal basis, keeping everything consistent. The core orbitals are naturally eigenstates of the ion Hamiltonian, so the sum over intermediate states stays orthogonal to them automatically — but since the entrant orbital comes from the neutral atom, it isn't itself an eigenstate of the ion potential, so it won't be perfectly orthogonal to those intermediate states, which is a subtlety I should flag. One alternative is to instead define the entrant orbital as an eigenstate of the ion potential itself, making the whole basis orthonormal, though I need to check whether the specification actually calls for that.

Since dipole selection rules mean the intermediate states differ in angular momentum from the entrant orbital, there's no overlap problem to worry about there. For the other sum, where angular momentum could coincide with occupied core shells, those shells are excluded as they're already filled, but the entrant orbital's own partially-filled shell should still be included since Pauli exclusion only applies fractionally.

I'm also working out the "ns2 excluded" rule for d-block atoms — identifying the outermost s-shell whose principal quantum number exceeds the valence n, which applies to Sc, Y, and La but not Cs. Then I'm estimating the computational cost: for each core shell and each box state in the relevant angular momentum channels, I need to compute Y1 integrals on the mesh, then combine these into R^1 matrix elements — with roughly 200 states per channel, this becomes a sizable but tractable matrix calculation.

I'm checking that the box has enough states below 3 Ha given a mesh extending to 300 au, finding around 230 states per angular momentum channel, and confirming the energy denominators stay positive. For the adiabatic closure term, I realize I need to sum over the full set of box states (not just those below 3 Ha) for the inner shell, so I'm setting up that separate closure calculation.

Sternheimer projected out occupied core orbitals, and corepol did the same while using a coarse r_e ladder, giving E_A_closed = −0.02985 for Cs, which I'm treating as within 10% of my own result. Now comparing PN4's use of corepol's E_A against my nonadiabatic calculation with the eps<3 cutoff, I need to account for truncating the a-sum at 3 Ha.

I'll also compute the closure sum with the same truncation to isolate the truncation loss, reporting both values, noting E2 is negative (attractive) while SPEC reports magnitudes.

Setting up the radial grid and tridiagonal matrix for the Sternheimer equation...

Symmetrizing the tridiagonal system and converting back to the physical wavefunction with proper normalization, then checking the accuracy of the log-mesh finite-difference scheme against the expected grid spacing.

I'm working out the Hartree potential Y1 via cumulative integrals, using cumsum to handle the inner and outer radial integration pieces efficiently.

Then I'm computing the exchange-like matrix element R1 by contracting Y1 against the weighted wavefunction overlap, and assembling the second-order energy correction from R1 squared divided by the energy denominators across the relevant shells.

I need to handle occupied-state exclusion carefully: for each l, I exclude the lowest shells that are already occupied in the ion core, since those box states duplicate existing orbitals, while the entrant shell remains allowed since it's empty in the ion. Then I'm setting up the adiabatic closure approximation, summing over the full set of a-states (excluding occupied ones) with a simplified energy denominator that lets the b-sum close via completeness.

For the non-adiabatic case, I want to truncate the a-sum at some energy cutoff and check the closure result against that same truncation to see how much it matters. I also need to define the entrant's energy consistently as its expectation value in the ion's reference Hamiltonian, matching how the denominators are used elsewhere, and confirm this holds for the cesium case specifically.

"""drow_n.py -- s30 Route N (PREDICTION-DROW-SESSION-30). Non-adiabatic second-order entrant-core correlation, dipole (k=1) direct term,
in the ion HFS local potential of the chain (corepol.orbitals). Basis = box eigenstates of h_l on the log mesh (symmetric tridiagonal, phi = r g),
same discretisation as corepol.sternheimer. E2 = -(1/3) sum_i N_i sum_{a,b} f_ia f_eb R1(ie;ab)^2 / (eps_a+eps_b-eps_i-eps_e).
a excludes ion-occupied shells of l_a (entrant shell allowed: empty in the ion); b excludes ion-occupied shells of l_b. Box cut eps < ECUT (3 Ha) stated.
Adiabatic gate: drop (eps_b-eps_e), close over b -> must reproduce corepol E_A_closed (Sternheimer, exact a-sum) on Cs within 10 %.
usage: python3 drow_n.py Z [Z ...]  -> drow_n.jsonl (done-set)."""
import sys,os,json,numpy as np,time
from scipy.linalg import eigh_tridiagonal
from t5_scf import ground_occ,minus
import corepol as CP
SH=CP.SH; ECUT=3.0; LMAX=4
def box(Vr,r,h,l):
    d=(1.0/h**2+0.125+l*(l+1)/2.0+Vr*r*r)/(r*r); e=(-0.5/h**2)/(r[:-1]*r[1:])
    w,phi=eigh_tridiagonal(d,e); U=(phi/np.sqrt(h*r)[:,None]).T   # rows = states, u normalised: int u^2 dr = 1
    return w,U
def Y1(rho,r,dr):
    """Y1[rho](r) = r^-2 int_0^r rho r' dr' + r int_r^inf rho r'^-2 dr'  (rows of rho)."""
    a=np.cumsum(rho*(r*dr),axis=1); b=np.cumsum((rho*(dr/(r*r)))[:,::-1],axis=1)[:,::-1]
    return a/(r*r)+b*r
def fac(l,lp): return max(l,lp)/(2*l+1)
def run(Z):
    el,sh=SH[Z]; n,l=int(sh[0]),"spdf".index(sh[1]); occ=ground_occ(Z); ion=minus(occ,n,l,1.0)
    x,r,h,dr=CP.mesh(Z); Vn,Pn=CP.orbitals(Z,occ,1); ue=Pn[(n,l)][0]
    Vi,Pi=CP.orbitals(Z,ion,1); Vr=Vi(r)
    amax=max(a for a,b,q in ion if b==0); ns={(a,b) for a,b,q in ion if b==0 and a==amax and a>n}
    nocc={}                                                             # ion-occupied shells per l -> count (lowest box states excluded)
    for a,b,q in ion: nocc[b]=nocc.get(b,0)+1
    B={}                                                                # box per l: (eps, U) with occupied removed, and full for gate
    for lb in range(LMAX+1):
        w,U=box(Vr,r,h,lb); k=nocc.get(lb,0); B[lb]=dict(full=(w,U),free=(w[k:],U[k:]),occ_e=w[:k])
    # entrant energy in the ion potential
    d=(1.0/h**2+0.125+l*(l+1)/2.0+Vr*r*r)/(r*r); e=(-0.5/h**2)/(r[:-1]*r[1:]); phi=ue*np.sqrt(h*r)
    eps_e=float(np.sum(d*phi*phi)+2*np.sum(e*phi[:-1]*phi[1:]))
    # eigenvalue check: box bound states vs numerov ion orbitals
    dev=max(abs(B[b]['occ_e'][ [aa for aa,bb,qq in ion if bb==b].index(a) if False else 0 ]-0) for a,b,q in ion) if False else 0.0
    chk=[]
    for a,b,q in ion:
        idx=sorted(aa for aa,bb,qq in ion if bb==b).index(a); chk.append(abs(B[b]['occ_e'][idx]-Pi[(a,b)][1]))
    dev=float(max(chk))
    out=dict(Z=Z,el=el,sh=sh,eps_e_ion=round(eps_e,5),eps_e_neu=round(float(Pn[(n,l)][1]),5),box_dev_max=round(dev,5),ecut=ECUT,npts=len(r))
    tot={'closed':0.0,'ns':0.0}; ad_full={'closed':0.0,'ns':0.0}; ad_cut={'closed':0.0,'ns':0.0}; nb={}
    ue2=ue*ue
    for (ni,li,Ni) in ion:
        ui,ei,_=Pi[(ni,li)]; grp='ns' if (ni,li) in ns else 'closed'
        for la in (li-1,li+1):
            if la<0 or la>LMAX: continue
            fia=fac(li,la)
            for tag,(wa,Ua) in (('full',B[la]['full']),('cut',None)):
                pass
            wa,Ua=B[la]['free']; sel=wa<ECUT
            rho=ui[None,:]*Ua; Ya=Y1(rho,r,dr)                    # all free a (for the full adiabatic closure)
            Da=wa-ei
            # adiabatic closure over b (sum_lb f_eb = 1): sum_a (1/Da) int ue^2 Ya^2 dr
            I=(Ya*Ya)@(ue2*dr)
            ad_full[grp]+=-(1.0/3.0)*Ni*fia*float(np.sum(I/Da)); ad_cut[grp]+=-(1.0/3.0)*Ni*fia*float(np.sum((I/Da)[sel]))
            Ya=Ya[sel]; Da=Da[sel]
            for lb in (l-1,l+1):
                if lb<0 or lb>LMAX: continue
                feb=fac(l,lb); wb,Ub=B[lb]['free']; sb=wb<ECUT; wb=wb[sb]; Ub=Ub[sb]; nb[lb]=int(sb.sum())
                W=(ue[None,:]*Ub)*dr[None,:]; R1=Ya@W.T                                     # (n_a x n_b)
                D=Da[:,None]+(wb-eps_e)[None,:]
                tot[grp]+=-(1.0/3.0)*Ni*fia*feb*float(np.sum(R1*R1/D))
    out.update(E2_closed=round(tot['closed'],5),E2_ns=round(tot['ns'],5),adiab_closed_full=round(ad_full['closed'],5),adiab_closed_cut=round(ad_cut['closed'],5),
               adiab_ns_full=round(ad_full['ns'],5),n_b=nb,ns_shells=sorted(ns))
    return out
if __name__=="__main__":
    OUT="drow_n.jsonl"; done={d['Z'] for d in map(json.loads,open(OUT))} if os.path.exists(OUT) else set()
    for Z in map(int,sys.argv[1:]):
        if Z in done: print("SKIP",Z); continue
        t0=time.time(); o=run(Z); o['sec']=int(time.time()-t0)
        open(OUT,"a").write(json.dumps(o)+"\n"); print(o,flush=True)

    dev=max(abs(B[b]['occ_e'][ [aa for aa,bb,qq in ion if bb==b].index(a) if False else 0 ]-0) for a,b,q in ion) if False else 0.0
    chk=[]

    dev=float(max(chk))

    tot={'closed':0.0,'ns':0.0}; ad_full={'closed':0.0,'ns':0.0}; ad_cut={'closed':0.0,'ns':0.0}; nb={}
    ue2=ue*ue
    for (ni,li,Ni) in ion:
        ui,ei,_=Pi[(ni,li)]; grp='ns' if (ni,li) in ns else 'closed'
        for la in (li-1,li+1):
            if la<0 or la>LMAX: continue
            fia=fac(li,la)
            for tag,(wa,Ua) in (('full',B[la]['full']),('cut',None)):
                pass
            wa,Ua=B[la]['free']; sel=wa<ECUT
            rho=ui[None,:]*Ua; Ya=Y1(rho,r,dr)                    # all free a (for the full adiabatic closure)
            Da=wa-ei
            # adiabatic closure over b (sum_lb f_eb = 1): sum_a (1/Da) int ue^2 Ya^2 dr
            I=(Ya*Ya)@(ue2*dr)
            ad_full[grp]+=-(1.0/3.0)*Ni*fia*float(np.sum(I/Da)); ad_cut[grp]+=-(1.0/3.0)*Ni*fia*float(np.sum((I/Da)[sel]))
            Ya=Ya[sel]; Da=Da[sel]
            for lb in (l-1,l+1):

                feb=fac(l,lb); wb,Ub=B[lb]['free']; sb=wb<ECUT; wb=wb[sb]; Ub=Ub[sb]; nb[lb]=int(sb.sum())
                W=(ue[None,:]*Ub)*dr[None,:]; R1=Ya@W.T                                     # (n_a x n_b)
                D=Da[:,None]+(wb-eps_e)[None,:]

I'm breaking down the self-interaction correction as the total-density GB term minus the sum of each shell's own-density GB contribution, then decomposing the change in correlation energy between f=1 and f=0 into three pieces: the restricted total-density term within the cutoff radius, the entrant's own-density SIC term, and whatever gets removed beyond the cutoff.

Working within the f=1 SCF density, I'm treating the entrant electron as having spin-up density only with zero spin-down, so its self-term is just the correlation energy functional evaluated on that single-electron density — and since this term is subtracted in the total correlation energy, it actually raises E_c overall. I'm also noting that since the correlation energy density is clipped to zero beyond the cutoff radius by construction, the "removed" piece isn't captured within the restricted term itself but would need to come from comparing against an unclipped version beyond that radius.

I'm setting up the decomposition so that the frozen-density pieces plus a relaxation residual sum to the total correlation energy shift, with that shift expected to be negative since correlation strengthens in the neutral atom, and I'm tracking an excess of roughly 0.009 across yttrium, lanthanum, and lutetium. For the second prediction, I want to relate this excess to the entrant charge sitting between the peak of the penultimate shell's density and the cutoff radius, checking whether that ratio stays roughly constant — within about 20% — across the row, which would point to a geometric origin. I'm also committing to the prediction that the self-term contribution should always come out positive, since the correlation energy density itself is never positive.

Now I'm reconsidering whether that positivity claim is actually a meaningful test, and instead trying to predict the magnitude: I expect this self-term to be comparable to the excess for yttrium, lanthanum, and lutetium, but smaller for scandium — except that scandium's compact 3d shell implies a higher local density for the entrant electron, which by the high-density correlation energy form would actually make this term larger for scandium, not smaller. That flips my expectation, suggesting the ordering should be scandium greater than yttrium, roughly equal to lanthanum and lutetium, which would mean the shape test fails for scandium and that the deficit isn't simply explained by the entrant's own self-interaction correction.

I'm also checking the residual against a relaxation threshold of 0.005 Ha across all rows, then computing the P2 ratio of excess to Q_gap — working out excess values for Y, La, Lu, and Sc from their missing/required fractions, and now figuring out where the entrant charge gap falls relative to the cutoff radius for each element.

Looking at the gap charge estimates, Sc's ratio comes out far smaller than Y's, so the ratios aren't constant across the row — but Y, La, and Lu stay within about 30% of each other, which points toward Route N being the right physical picture. I still need to work out the E2 form and add an adiabatic-limit gate checking against the closed-shell core polarization energy within 10%.

Thinking through the SPEC's completeness check: dropping the energy denominator difference and summing over intermediate states should reproduce the Sternheimer-based core polarization result, but a finite box with continuum states capped below 3 Ha might not saturate that sum. I expect the gate only passes if continuum states are included, with bound-state-only sums falling well short — maybe under 50%. I'll commit to testing whether the adiabatic-limit sum over box states reproduces the core polarization energy within 10%, and if not, report the fractional shortfall as evidence of basis incompleteness. I also want to check whether the two-electron matrix element used in SPEC N2 …

# PREDICTION — the d-row excess (SPEC-DROW-EXCESS-SESSION-30), BOTH routes. Written BEFORE any run. s30, 2026-08-17.
# Rulings in force: SUBCELL=1; correlation = the one function I on the sc path; adiabatic A closed; Cs settled (cut region == core-valence region);
# comparison decides; no scan; no constant. Inputs: cutfrac.jsonl / frachf.jsonl (s29), banked meas/so columns only. Cs/Y RECALLED-NOT-ENTERED.
# The object: excess = missing - F_out*required (Ha):  Y 0.0102 · La 0.0071 · Lu 0.0085 · Sc 0.0014 · (Cs 0 by definition of B). Gd set aside (4f-adjacent).

## Route P — object property of the local form? (drow_p.py, extends cutfrac's f=1 neutral SCF; DEc_sc NOT re-derived)
Decomposition on the f=1 SCF densities, frozen (core = total - entrant): (a) = int_{r<r_cut} [n eps_c(n) - n_core eps_c(n_core)] (total-density GB piece
owed to the entrant, inside the domain); (b) = - int n_e eps_c(n_e,0) (the entrant's own PZ SIC term, as E_c subtracts it; > 0 by construction);
(c) = int_{r>r_cut} [n e_unclip(n) - n_core e_unclip(n_core)] (what the eps_c>=0 cut removes; e_unclip = GB form without the zero clip);
relax = DEc_sc - (a) - (b) (what the two-SCF difference holds beyond the frozen pieces: core-SIC and self-density relaxation).
PP1  (b) is NOT the excess. Committed: (b) on Sc >= (b) on Y >= (b) on La ~ (b) on Lu (own-density order, Sc most compact); |(b)| in [0.005, 0.05] Ha
     on all four; the SHAPE (Sc small, Y La Lu ~equal) does not hold. If instead (b) on Y La Lu is in [0.005,0.015] AND (b)_Sc < 0.4*(b)_Y, P1 HOLDS
     and the deficit is the entrant's own SIC over-subtracting in the core -> object property, statable.
PP1b relax closes: |relax| < 0.005 Ha on every row (frozen decomposition accounts for DEc_sc to that bound). Failure -> the pieces are not additive
     and (a)/(b) may not be quoted against the excess without the relaxation term.
PP1c (c) on Cs >= 0.010 Ha (the cut IS Cs); (c) on d rows <= 0.004 Ha (the cut is not the d-row object) — restates B from the density side.
PP2  ratio = excess / Q_gap, Q_gap = entrant charge with r_peak((n-1)p) < r < r_cut. Committed: NOT a single number — Sc ratio < 0.3 * min(Y,La,Lu);
     Y La Lu ratios agree to within 30 % of each other. If all four agree within 20 %: geometric (form-domain), state it. Else -> physics, Route N decides.
Prediction of the route outcome: P says NOT "domain of the form" (PP1 shape fails, PP2 fails on Sc). If both hold instead, that is a finding against me.

## Route N — non-adiabatic entrant-core second order (drow_n.py on the shooter's HFS-SR ion potential; the chain's own basis)
N1 basis: bound l=0..3 to eps > -1e-3 plus box continuum on the log mesh, eps < +3 Ha, stated by count per l. N2: E2 = - sum_i sum_{a,b} |<ie|1/r12|ab>|^2/D
with k=1 dipole Slater integral, direct term only, i in the closed core ((n-1)s2p6 inward; ns2 excluded and reported), e = HFS entrant.
NG1 basis gate: adiabatic limit (drop eps_b-eps_e, sum over b) reproduces corepol Cs E_A_closed (-0.02985 uncoupled-Xalpha scale) within 10 %.
     If bound-only falls short by > 30 %, that is the continuum's share and is reported as such, not as a failure of N.
PN1 (SPEC N3) E2(closed) Y La Lu in [0.005, 0.015] Ha; Sc <= 0.003; Cs in [0.008, 0.02] (one object with B).  PN2 ratio Sc/Y < 0.3.
PN3 order Y >= Lu >= La (larger, more polarisable (n-1)s2p6 shell against a diffuser entrant; La's 5p is the largest, but its 5d is the most diffuse —

I'm catching an inconsistency in the peak labeling — for the 3d entrant like Sc, (n−1)p should mean 2p, but the core being referenced is actually the Ar-like 3s3p shell, so I need to reconcile which core level the notation is actually pointing to.

For d-row entrants, the convention should use the same-n s2p6 shell (3s3p for Sc, 4s4p for Y, 5s5p for La/Lu), meaning n should track the valence-s principal number rather than the entrant's own n. My code is using the entrant's n directly, which gives 2p for Sc instead of the correct 3p — and the numbers confirm this, since the computed peak value of 0.232 is way too small for a 3p peak (which should be closer to 0.7). This is a real bug I caught by checking the output against expectations, not something I noticed before running the calculation.…

{"returncode":0,"stdout":""""drow_n.py -- s30 Route N (PREDICTION-DROW-SESSION-30). Non-adiabatic second-order entrant-core correlation, dipole (k=1) direct term,
in the ion HFS local potential of the chain (corepol.orbitals). Basis = box eigenstates of h_l on the log mesh (symmetric tridiagonal, phi = r g),
same discretisation as corepol.sternheimer. E2 = -(1/3) sum_i N_i sum_{a,b} f_ia f_eb R1(ie;ab)^2 / (eps_a+eps_b-eps_i-eps_e).
a excludes ion-occupied shells of l_a (entrant shell allowed: empty in the ion); b excludes ion-occupied shells of l_b. Box cut eps < ECUT (3 Ha) stated.
Adiabatic gate: drop (eps_b-eps_e), close over b -> must reproduce corepol E_A_closed (Sternheimer, exact a-sum) on Cs within 10 %.
usage: python3 drow_n.py Z [Z ...]  -> drow_n.jsonl (done-set)."""
import sys,os,json,numpy as np,time
from scipy.linalg import eigh_tridiagonal
from t5_scf import ground_occ,minus
import corepol as CP
SH=CP.SH; ECUT=3.0; LMAX=4
def box(Vr,r,h,l):
    d=(1.0/h**2+0.125+l*(l+1)/2.0+Vr*r*r)/(r*r); e=(-0.5/h**2)/(r[:-1]*r[1:])
    w,phi=eigh_tridiagonal(d,e); U=(phi/np.sqrt(h*r)[:,None]).T   # rows = states, u normalised: int u^2 dr = 1
    return w,U
def Y1(rho,r,dr):
    """Y1[rho](r) = r^-2 int_0^r rho r' dr' + r int_r^inf rho r'^-2 dr'  (rows of rho)."""
    a=np.cumsum(rho*(r*dr),axis=1); b=np.cumsum((rho*(dr/(r*r)))[:,::-1],axis=1)[:,::-1]
    return a/(r*r)+b*r
def fac(l,lp): return max(l,lp)/(2*l+1)
def run(Z):
    el,sh=SH[Z]; n,l=int(sh[0]),"spdf".index(sh[1]); occ=ground_occ(Z); ion=minus(occ,n,l,1.0)
    x,r,h,dr=CP.mesh(Z); Vn,Pn=CP.orbitals(Z,occ,1); ue=Pn[(n,l)][0]
    Vi,Pi=CP.orbitals(Z,ion,1); Vr=Vi(r)
    amax=max(a for a,b,q in ion if b==0); ns={(a,b) for a,b,q in ion if b==0 and a==amax and a>n}
    nocc={}                                                             # ion-occupied shells per l -> count (lowest box states excluded)
    for a,b,q in ion: nocc[b]=nocc.get(b,0)+1
    B={}                                                                # box per l: (eps, U) with occupied removed, and full for gate
    for lb in range(LMAX+1):
        w,U=box(Vr,r,h,lb); k=nocc.get(lb,0); B[lb]=dict(full=(w,U),free=(w[k:],U[k:]),occ_e=w[:k])
    # entrant energy in the ion potential
    d=(1.0/h**2+0.125+l*(l+1)/2.0+Vr*r*r)/(r*r); e=(-0.5/h**2)/(r[:-1]*r[1:]); phi=ue*np.sqrt(h*r)
    eps_e=float(np.sum(d*phi*phi)+2*np.sum(e*phi[:-1]*phi[1:]))
    # eigenvalue check: box bound states vs numerov ion orbitals
    chk=[]
    for a,b,q in ion:
        idx=sorted(aa for aa,bb,qq in ion if bb==b).index(a); chk.append(abs(B[b]['occ_e'][idx]-Pi[(a,b)][1]))
    dev=float(max(chk))
    out=dict(Z=Z,el=el,sh=sh,eps_e_ion=round(eps_e,5),eps_e_neu=round(float(Pn[(n,l)][1]),5),box_dev_max=round(dev,5),ecut=ECUT,npts=len(r))
    tot={'closed':0.0,'ns':0.0}; ad_full={'closed':0.0,'ns':0.0}; ad_cut={'closed':0.0,'ns':0.0}; nb={}
    ue2=ue*ue
    for (ni,li,Ni) in ion:
        ui,ei,_=Pi[(ni,li)]; grp='ns' if (ni,li) in ns else 'closed'
        for la in (li-1,li+1):
            if la<0 or la>LMAX: continue
            fia=fac(li,la)
            wa,Ua=B[la]['free']; sel=wa<ECUT
            rho=ui[None,:]*Ua; Ya=Y1(rho,r,dr)                    # all free a (for the full adiabatic closure)
            Da=wa-ei
            # adiabatic closure over b (sum_lb f_eb = 1): sum_a (1/Da) int ue^2 Ya^2 dr
            I=(Ya*Ya)@(ue2*dr)
            ad_full[grp]+=-(1.0/3.0)*Ni*fia*float(np.sum(I/Da)); ad_cut[grp]+=-(1.0/3.0)*Ni*fia*float(np.sum((I/Da)[sel]))
            Ya=Ya[sel]; Da=Da[sel]
            for lb in (l-1,l+1):
                if lb<0 or lb>LMAX: continue
                feb=fac(l,lb); wb,Ub=B[lb]['free']; sb=wb<ECUT; wb=wb[sb]; Ub=Ub[sb]; nb[lb]=int(sb.sum())

from scipy.linalg import eigh_tridiagonal
from t5_scf import ground_occ,minus
import corepol as CP
SH=CP.SH; ECUT=3.0; LMAX=4
def box(Vr,r,h,l):
    d=(1.0/h**2+0.125+l*(l+1)/2.0+Vr*r*r)/(r*r); e=(-0.5/h**2)/(r[:-1]*r[1:])
    w,phi=eigh_tridiagonal(d,e); U=(phi/np.sqrt(h*r)[:,None]).T   # rows = states, u normalised: int u^2 dr = 1
    return w,U
def Y1(rho,r,dr):
    """Y1[rho](r) = r^-2 int_0^r rho r' dr' + r int_r^inf rho r'^-2 dr'  (rows of rho)."""
    a=np.cumsum(rho*(r*dr),axis=1); b=np.cumsum((rho*(dr/(r*r)))[:,::-1],axis=1)[:,::-1]
    return a/(r*r)+b*r
def fac(l,lp): return max(l,lp)/(2*l+1)
def run(Z):
    el,sh=SH[Z]; n,l=int(sh[0]),"spdf".index(sh[1]); occ=ground_occ(Z); ion=minus(occ,n,l,1.0)
    x,r,h,dr=CP.mesh(Z); Vn,Pn=CP.orbitals(Z,occ,1); ue=Pn[(n,l)][0]
    Vi,Pi=CP.orbitals(Z,ion,1); Vr=Vi(r)

    nocc={}                                                             # ion-occupied shells per l -> count (lowest box states excluded)
    for a,b,q in ion: nocc[b]=nocc.get(b,0)+1

content.thinking:
I'm double-checking the sign logic: with a shallower eps_e, the gap eps_b minus eps_e shrinks, which makes the overall denominator D smaller and pushes E2's magnitude larger — confirming that a shallower entrant elasticity leads to a bigger E2.

Neither convention gets E2 close to the target 0.009, since the closed-core dipole term sits at 0.03–0.05 across all d-row elements including Sc, so PN1 fails consistently. The ns2 term blows up under the neu convention due to near-degenerate denominators, but that's a separate valence-valence correlation effect, not part of this core term.

Looking at Route N's structure, the entrant-core second-order term shows up on 3d about as strongly as on 4d/5d, which doesn't match the excess's shape since Sc lacks that excess — so this isn't the missing physics either. Both routes failing supports treating this as a genuinely new object, though I should consider whether Route N's failure stems from build limitations like the uncoupled ×1.8 scaling or missing exchange terms, since exchange would act with opposite sign relative to direct.

I'm also realizing the local correlation form already captures much of this core-valence correlation — the coupled E2 value (0.02–0.03) is comparable to what's already delivered by the local form, meaning E2 represents the whole correlation rather than the missing 0.009. The proper comparison is coupled E2 against the total required correlation (~0.028–0.033): for Sc, 0.028 required versus 0.026 delivered is already 93%, so this second-order term can't honestly be read as the residual — it's the same size as what's already accounted for.

Looking at Sc more carefully, the local form delivers 93% at 3d but only 61–65% at 4d/5d, which points to something physically different between these cases: the nd≥4 orbitals have radial nodes (4d has one, 5d has two) while 3d is nodeless, so the inner lobes of 4d/5d overlap with the core shell in a way 3d doesn't.

This node count could be the real discriminator here — local correlation depends only on density, and the self-interaction correction of the entering orbital subtracts self-correlation differently depending on whether there's a node. Rather than just fitting this, I should treat it as a testable prediction: split B into inner-lobe (inside the node) and outer-lobe contributions and see if the inner-lobe piece behaves differently across noded versus nodeless cases.…

K. A. Brueckner · The quantity εc is defined as the correlation energy per particle of an electron gas expressed in rydbergs. It is a function of the conventional dimensionless parameter rs, where rs-3 is proportional to the electron density. Here εc is computed for small values of rs (high density) and found to be given by εc=Alnrs+C+O(rs). # Correlation energy of an electron gas in strong magnetic fields at high densities

M.Steinberg, J. Ortner

Institut für Physik, Humboldt Universität zu Berlin, Invalidenstr. 110, D-10115 Berlin, Germany (October 18, 2018)

The high-density electron gas in a strong magnetic field B and at zero temperature is investigated. The quantum strong-field limit is considered in which only the lowest Landau level is occupied. It is shown that the perturbation series of the ground-state energy can be represented in analogy to the Gell-Mann Brueckner expression of the ground-state energy of the field-free electron gas. The role of the expansion parameter is taken by $r_B = (2/3\pi^2) (B/m^2) (\hbar r_S/e)^3$ instead of the field-free Gell-Mann Brueckner parameter $r_s$ . The perturbation series is given exactly up to $o(r_B)$ for the case of a small filling factor for the lowest Landau level.

Search done — and the candidate was hiding in plain sight, in our own s23 file.

**Literature:** Nozières & Pines (Phys. Rev. 111, 442, 1958) state the Gell-Mann–Brueckner high-density result is valid only for r_s ≲ 1. Our chain's correlation form is exactly that truncated expansion, λ₀ ln r_s + ε₀ (+E0B), evaluated at valence densities r_s ≈ 1.5 (Sc 3d) to 2.5–3 (Y/La/Lu nd) to 4–6 (Cs 6s).

**Numbers (Ry/electron, ζ=0), our own code:**

r_s | GB-truncated (chain) | full RPA ring (ring_zeta.py, s23) | Ceperley-Alder
1 | −0.094 | −0.158 | −0.120
2 | −0.051 | −0.124 | −0.090
3 | −0.025 | −0.101* | −0.074
4 | −0.008 | — | −0.064

The truncation delivers 78 % of the correlation at r_s=1, 56 % at r_s=2, 34 % at r_s=3, 12 % at r_s=4, and hits zero near r_s=5 — that is the cut. So mechanism B (the cut) on Cs and the "missing inside the domain" on the d rows are one object: the expansion falls away long before it reaches zero, and how far it falls is set by the entrant's r_s. Sc's compact 3d sits where the form still holds; the diffuser nd≥4 rows do not. This is the discriminator every test today failed to find, and it is a property of the form, not of the atoms.

The full ring sum (BRM 2024 integrand, already derived in-project for ε₀) is valid at all r_s and needs no cut; it overbinds by an almost r_s-independent ≈0.035 Ry, which is what the second-order exchange constant E0B (Onsager, already in the chain) supplies. Ring + E0B gives −0.110 (r_s=1) and −0.076 (r_s=2) against CA −0.120/−0.090 — ~90 % everywhere instead of 78 %→12 %. No constant chosen; the only numerics are ring_zeta's grids (a nan-mask at K~1e-4, X~1000 was needed at finite r_s — cancellation in g, not physics; masked value at r_s=1 matches the literature RPA −0.157 Ry).

**Candidate C, for ruling:** replace the truncated expansion by the tabulated full ring eps_r(r_s,ζ) + E0B pointwise (same SIC structure, same everything else), corr='R'; predictions to file first, then the six class rows on the frachf path, comparison against corr='Z' decides.     ir=np.clip(np.searchsorted(LR,lr)-1,0,len(LR)-2); tr=(lr-LR[ir])/(LR[ir+1]-LR[ir])

The excess_R check fails for Y (0.0051 vs 0.004 threshold) though La and Lu pass. For the deliverable-ratio test, Sc overshoots by 15% while Y, La, Lu remain 6-15% short — so the ring-form truncation adds a roughly uniform boost across all rows rather than resolving the Sc-vs-others discrepancy, though it does shrink the Sc/(Y,La,Lu) ratio from 1.50 to 1.30, suggesting truncation explains part but not all of the shortfall.

I'm now reasoning that since both an overbinding form and an underbinding form bracket the exact uniform-electron-gas result yet both preserve the same class contrast between Sc and the nd≥4 elements, this points to a genuine non-local property beyond standard LDA for those nd≥4 rows rather than an artifact of the radial form. I'm also tracking the residual values (measurement plus spin-orbit plus total-density corrections) across elements under different functional forms to see if this pattern holds.…
